All 14 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (as_is).  14 of 14 named artefacts have been revised or had their bytes replaced since this review was issued, so this record is re-issued at revision 2 and its digest for those artefacts now names the current revision; per-artefact detail, including the superseded digest and the basis for each classification, is in digest_corrections. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. scope: PARTIAL SCOPE, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE POINT. FB2-VER-EXE-000001 is excluded because a concurrent session revised it to revision 2 with different content during this review pass; a challenge pass that asserts findings against content that is being rewritten underneath it would manufacture false assurance. CONCURRENT MODIFICATION, MATERIAL: while this review pass was running, another session was actively rewriting the as_is verification population. FB2-VER-EXE-000001 was revised from revision 1 to revision 2 with different content (its recorded sha256 changed from 3db888bd67f66ccd57674e7b365c64ae45ddbd5ca378d86f52c05833aac963c0 to 452089f34c...), as were FB2-VER-EXE-000002..000005, and eight further as_is execution records (FB2-VER-EXE-000006..000014) were created. The corpus artifact index grew from 87 to 131 entries and the validator's finding count moved from 21 to 30 during this pass. This review therefore EXCLUDES every as_is execution artifact from its scope and states that exclusion rather than asserting findings about content that is in motion. The sixteen as_is artifacts enumerated in reviewed_ids below were each re-hashed after the concurrent writes and are byte-stable at the digests recorded. The 16 as_is artifacts listed below are exactly the stable remainder of the chain FB2-REV-000001 declared, namely that review's 17 reviewed_ids minus FB2-VER-EXE-000001. This record is not a universal review of the as_is profile.

findings.description: Independent confirmation of FB2-REV-000001 finding FB2-FND-000001, with the arithmetic corrected. That finding stated the chain as '100 ms period + 10 ms SOA check + 5 ms contactor = 115 ms > FTTI 100 ms'. Re-derived from the requirement statements themselves: FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 requires acquisition at a minimum rate of 20 Hz with publication within 25 ms, so a 20 Hz period is 50 ms and the acquisition leg is up to 50 + 25 = 75 ms, not 100 ms; FB2-SAF-FSR-000002 requires classification within 5 ms of data availability but also a debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms, which adds a further sample wait; FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 requires contactor opening within 30 ms. The conclusion that the main path does not fit inside a 100 ms FTTI holds and is in fact worse than the earlier review stated, because the earlier figures used a 10 Hz period and omitted the debounce wait. The finding is upheld with corrected numbers; the original review record was not edited by this pass.
findings.evidence: FB2-SAF-FSR-000001 (as_is): 'acquire all cell voltages from AFE slaves at a minimum rate of 20 Hz with PEC/CRC validation, and publish validated data to the database within 25 ms of acquisition trigger'. FB2-SAF-FSR-000002: 'debounce of 2 consecutive violations within 100 ms, and classify violations within 5 ms of data availability'. FB2-SAF-FSR-000003: 'open all HV contactors within 30 ms of FAULT state request'. FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 sets FTTI 100 ms. Worst-case acquisition leg 50+25=75 ms, then classification 5 ms plus a debounce sample wait, then contactor 30 ms.

findings.description: The safety goal is ASIL_D with no asil_justification, so the classification driving the whole downstream chain is underived. The same condition is reported for the synthetic profile by FB2-REV-FND-000162. The validity of that requirement is load-bearing here in a way it is not elsewhere: FB2-REV-FND-000171 shows the chain does not meet a 100 ms FTTI, and FSR-000004 was introduced as an ASIL B parallel path specifically to address that. An ASIL D goal with no recorded derivation, whose chain does not meet its FTTI and is rescued by a lower-classification parallel path, is the weakest point in the as_is safety argument.
findings.evidence: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 (as_is): asil 'ASIL_D', asil_justification absent; reported by the corpus MUT-009 ASIL validator for this profile. FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 (as_is profile equivalent FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 is synthetic; the as_is chain stops at FSR-000003) - see FB2-REV-FND-000171 for the FTTI derivation.

findings.description: The prior review FB2-REV-000001 recorded digest 3db888bd67f66ccd57674e7b365c64ae45ddbd5ca378d86f52c05833aac963c0 for FB2-VER-EXE-000001. That artifact now hashes to a different value because a concurrent session revised it to revision 2. The prior review's digest entry is therefore stale as of this pass, which means the corpus's review record for the execution no longer binds to the content it was written against. This is precisely the stale-revision/stale-review condition the corpus's mutation scenario set is meant to exercise, and it is live in the baseline rather than injected. No tool check currently compares reviewed_ids digests against artifact content, so nothing in the corpus would have reported it. The prior record was NOT edited by this pass: correcting another reviewer's record is not this reviewer's to do, and master-prompt section 15 assigns repair to the artifact owner with confirmation by a further pass.
findings.evidence: FB2-REV-000001 reviewed_ids entry for FB2-VER-EXE-000001: digest 3db888bd67f66ccd57674e7b365c64ae45ddbd5ca378d86f52c05833aac963c0, revision '1'. Current file docs/artifacts/corpus/as_is/verification/execution-soa-voltage.json has revision '2' and a different sha256. corpus.py contains no check that recomputes reviewed_ids digests; the automated_review_coverage dimension only intersects artifact ids, never digests.

dispositions.action: Accepted and the earlier finding upheld with corrected arithmetic. The earlier review's conclusion stands; only its numbers were incomplete. FB2-REV-000001 was NOT edited by this pass.
Accepted. No ASIL was changed and no justification text was invented by this review. Referred to the safety owner.

Accepted as a live corpus-hygiene defect, not a historical curiosity. The prior review record was deliberately not edited. Remediation is either to re-review FB2-VER-EXE-000001 at its current revision and issue a new revision of the review, or to add a digest-recomputation check to the corpus tooling. Both are outside this review's write scope. Escalated as the highest-priority process finding of this pass.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).

This challenge pass was performed by the SAME automated session that produced the other review records in this pass. It examined artifacts that a different earlier session reviewed (FB2-REV-000001), but no independence mechanism exists between those two sessions. This is NOT organizational independence and NOT a qualified challenge function.
No test was executed and no target hardware was involved.

Verification performed: (a) the timing arithmetic in FB2-FND-000001 independently re-derived from the requirement statements; (b) all 16 in-scope artifacts re-hashed after the concurrent writes and confirmed byte-stable at the digests recorded here; (c) the ASIL justification condition confirmed for this profile; (d) the prior review's recorded digest for FB2-VER-EXE-000001 re-computed against current content and found to differ. (d) produced FB2-REV-FND-000174.
This pass did not re-review the 26 as_is deviation records (FB2-REV-000002) or the as_is test measures (FB2-REV-000006). No single record claims to cover the whole as_is profile.
